text: the phase machine (start, play, over) with the start screen and its prompt

comments.text: Blocking: The design defines four phases (`start`, `play`, `paused`, `over`), but Task 1 builds the phase machine with only three. Task 3 adds pause without saying it introduces the `paused` phase, or how P or Escape and blur/visibilitychange resume it (the design says P or Escape resumes). State in Task 1 that the machine includes `paused`, or say explicitly in Task 3 that it adds the phase and its transitions.

text: the game-over screen with the score, best score and restart prompt

comments.text: Task 2 shows the best score on the game-over screen, but storage and the best-score update are only added in Task 3 (the design updates best score on `over`). Task 2's A6 criterion therefore has no real best-score value to verify. Either state that Task 2 uses a placeholder in-memory best that Task 3 replaces with the storage wrappers, or move the best-score display to Task 3.

text: Pause triggers are P, Escape and `blur`/`visibilitychange`. P or Escape resumes (R8).

comments.text: The spec says pressing the same key resumes, and the design lets either P or Escape resume. A8 says 'the same holds for Escape', so pause with P then resume with Escape is untested and unclear. Also, after a blur-triggered pause there is no defined resume key. Define it, for example: any pause key resumes, and a blur-pause resumes on P or Escape.

text: The mute button is drawn on the canvas and hit-tested there, so no DOM image is needed.

comments.text: A tap on the canvas moves the cat, and the mute button sits on the same canvas. The design does not say that a tap on the button must toggle mute without also steering the cat or starting or restarting the game. Specify that the mute hit-test takes priority over movement and phase-advance handling, and add this to the A13 test.
